domain_setting: A welcoming bookshop, library, reading desk and publishing world. Each card should make the exact reading term clear through book form, paper, people or a restrained editorial setting.

ambient_palette.paper: warm ivory, cream and soft page shadows
ambient_palette.books: muted teal, blue, coral, ochre and plum covers without text or logos
ambient_palette.reading spaces: pale sage, warm wood, quiet shelf colors
ambient_palette.people: small calm figures with varied hair and clothing, keeping the book or action legible

recurring_scale_anchors: Canvas 304×192; show covers, pages, spines and hands at a readable size.
No lettering, readable titles, numbers, logos, brands or publisher marks.
When two terms are related, vary the physical format and composition so the distinction is immediate.
Avoid using the same open-book icon for every title or genre.
For biographies, visibly distinguish the person who writes from the person whose life is described.

polysemy_resolution_table.article: A written newspaper or magazine piece shown on a printed page with columns and a small photo, not a physical item or grammar article.
polysemy_resolution_table.autobiography / biography: Autobiography: the subject writes their own life story; biography: a separate writer documents another person’s life. Keep author and subject identities distinct.
polysemy_resolution_table.bestseller: A book selling in many copies, shown as a popular multi-copy display or busy shop stack; no readable bestseller badge or title.
polysemy_resolution_table.book: A general physical book with a visible cover and pages, distinct from formats and named reference books.
polysemy_resolution_table.novel: Fictional long-form story in a bound book, distinct from the adjective sense in the Japanese gloss.
polysemy_resolution_table.plot: A small, clearly bounded piece of land, shown as a surveyed lot with corner stakes and nearby plots; follow the Japanese gloss rather than the story-structure sense.
polysemy_resolution_table.cover: The outer cover of a book, not the verb meaning to put something over another object.
polysemy_resolution_table.spine: The human spinal column, shown as a centered chain of vertebrae within a simplified back-view torso; follow the Japanese gloss rather than the book-binding sense.
polysemy_resolution_table.romance: A love-story literary genre, shown as a book with a couple and heart motif; not the Romance-language family listed in the Japanese gloss.
polysemy_resolution_table.highbrow: An intellectual or culturally sophisticated reader in a quiet study, represented respectfully with scholarly books and art; avoid a literal raised eyebrow.
polysemy_resolution_table.coloring book: A bound activity book with blank outlined pictures meant to be colored, accompanied by crayons or colored pencils.
polysemy_resolution_table.comic: A printed comic book or graphic story with sequential panels, distinct from the adjective meaning funny.
polysemy_resolution_table.cookbook: A collection of recipes in a book, shown with food illustrations and cooking ingredients.
polysemy_resolution_table.course book: A textbook assigned as the principal reading or reference for a particular class.
polysemy_resolution_table.dictionary: A reference book organized into many short word-and-definition entries, suggested by indexed pages and guide tabs without visible letters.
polysemy_resolution_table.e-reader / e-book: E-reader is the dedicated electronic device with a screen and controls; e-book is digital book content, shown as a file or digital page.
polysemy_resolution_table.encyclopedia: A multi-volume or richly illustrated reference work covering many subjects, distinguished from the compact entries of a dictionary.
polysemy_resolution_table.gossip magazine: Glossy publication about public figures and social news, suggested with a celebrity collage and paparazzi camera, without readable covers.
polysemy_resolution_table.guidebook: Printed illustrated reference used to explore a destination; maps and landmarks should dominate over phrase translations.
polysemy_resolution_table.hardcover / hardback: A book with stiff protective boards and a visible rigid spine, contrasted with the flexible cover of a paperback.
polysemy_resolution_table.newspaper: A complete folded, multi-section daily or weekly news publication, shown as overlapping broadsheet pages; visually distinct from one standalone article.
polysemy_resolution_table.paperback: A book bound in a flexible paper cover, distinguished by its curled, thin cover edges from the rigid board cover of a hardcover.
polysemy_resolution_table.puzzles: Printed word or logic puzzles for readers to solve on a page, shown as a puzzle book with grids and pencil rather than a loose jigsaw-board toy.
polysemy_resolution_table.textbook: A school subject book with instructional diagrams and study tools; distinct from the course book illustration already adapted for a separate card.
polysemy_resolution_table.tv guide: A printed schedule for television programs, shown as a booklet with a color-block program grid and a small TV cue, not a TV set or transit timetable.
polysemy_resolution_table.audiobook: A book whose text is recorded and narrated aloud, shown by a book paired with headphones and sound waves.
polysemy_resolution_table.e-book: Digital book content shown as a downloadable book file on a screen, distinct from the dedicated e-reader device.
polysemy_resolution_table.crime fiction: A mystery or detective story as a book genre, with the book prominent and investigation clues secondary; not an actual crime scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.fantasy: A literary genre shown through an imaginative magical world emerging from a book; keep the book focal and avoid confusing it with science fiction.
polysemy_resolution_table.fiction: Writing that invents characters and events, illustrated by a storybook with a created character emerging from its page; broad category distinct from the specific novel form.
polysemy_resolution_table.humor: Writing intended to amuse, shown as a funny book illustration with a harmless visual gag rather than a comic strip or stand-up performance.
polysemy_resolution_table.nature writing: Literary writing inspired by close observation of the natural world, shown with a field notebook, writer’s pencil and living plants or wildlife.
polysemy_resolution_table.nonfiction / non-fiction: Writing about real people, places or events, suggested with documentary photographs and research tools, contrasting with invented stories.
polysemy_resolution_table.science fiction: A book genre imagining future science, technology or space travel, shown with a spacecraft and alien worlds; distinct from fantasy creatures and real laboratory science.
polysemy_resolution_table.self-help: Nonfiction advice that helps a reader improve their life or skills, shown as a book with a person progressing up clear steps.
polysemy_resolution_table.travel writing: Literary writing based on journeys and places, shown with a travel journal, map route, ticket and destination scene; distinct from travel directions.
polysemy_resolution_table.genre: A category of writing or literature, represented by different book types with clearly contrasting cover imagery.
polysemy_resolution_table.chapter: One major section of a longer book, suggested by a highlighted group of pages and a section marker within a thicker volume.
polysemy_resolution_table.headline: A prominent heading at the top of a newspaper or magazine story, shown as the largest band of a printed front page above smaller article columns.
polysemy_resolution_table.horoscope: An astrology forecast for a sign or period, shown as a magazine page with a zodiac wheel and constellation symbols.
polysemy_resolution_table.illustration: A picture printed within a book to accompany its content, distinct from a photo-led article page or the act of giving an example.
polysemy_resolution_table.page: One physical side of a leaf in a book or publication, shown as a single sheet with a lifted corner and a visible book edge.
polysemy_resolution_table.story: A narrative account of connected events, shown as a telling or an illustrated book scene; this chapter’s glossary emphasizes factual stories.
polysemy_resolution_table.author: The person who creates and writes a book, shown working on a manuscript beside a finished copy.
polysemy_resolution_table.reader: A person engaged with a book, with the person as the focal subject rather than the general reading activity.
polysemy_resolution_table.bookstore: A retail shop where customers browse and buy books; distinguish it from a library with a storefront display, shelves and a shopping bag.
polysemy_resolution_table.library: A public or school place for borrowing and reading books, shown with shelves and study space rather than sales displays.
polysemy_resolution_table.reading: The activity of reading a book, with the reader engaged at a desk and the open book visible; distinguish the setting from the reader-person card.
polysemy_resolution_table.flick through: Browse a publication rapidly by flicking and fanning several pages in quick succession.
polysemy_resolution_table.flip through: Browse a publication by lifting and turning its pages; use a single clearly curled page to distinguish the action from rapid page-fanning.
polysemy_resolution_table.glowing reviews: Several enthusiastic positive evaluations of a book, shown by the book beside multiple radiant star-rating cards; no readable words or numbers.
polysemy_resolution_table.page-turner: A highly absorbing book that keeps its reader engrossed, shown as the focal book with an excited late-night reader and pages in motion; distinguish the gripping book from the act of browsing pages.
